difficulty.label: 3.e5 player whose opponent breaks before developing

objective.summary: Black broke at your chain's base immediately, bishop still on c8. Take the pawn — the one answer that asks Black to prove the idea — and then make the real decision: hold the extra pawn with c3/b4, or hand it back at the moment that buys you the better game.

planClasses.label: Hold it (c3, b4, Be3)
planClasses.description: Position-specific arithmetic: the c5 pawn can be kept exactly as long as b4 is defensible against ...a5 and ...e6/...Bxc5 is met with a piece already there. Every extra holding move is a development move not played.

planClasses.label: Return it at a price
planClasses.description: The other option: give the pawn back rather than spend more moves holding it, keeping the e5 space and the development lead. This pack no longer authors a concrete line for it — the line it used to author (5.Be3 Bxc5 6.Bxc5) was refuted by the 2026-08-15 engine pass and removed.

annotations: The critical test, and the point of this pack: with Black's bishop still on c8, taking does not lose a tempo to anything. Black must now spend moves to regain the pawn — the exact opposite of the tempo race in the main-line Advance.
Note what happened to the structure: the d4-e5 chain this variation is named for is gone. You are no longer playing a chain position; you are playing a lead in development with an e5 space pawn.
The active try: develop and collect c5 later with the pieces. This is the version where holding the pawn is most ambitious and most testing for both sides.
Develop toward the kingside first. The c5 pawn is not running away, and every White piece that appears makes ...Nxe5 tricks less available.
Black's bishop finally moves — to pin the knight rather than to blockade. The pressure is real but it is aimed at your development, not at the c5 pawn.
The holding move: b4 is prepared, ...Qa5+ is blunted, and the b4/d4 squares are covered against the c6 knight. One pawn move that does three jobs is how a pawn gets held without falling behind.
Black finally bids for the pawn with the bishop's diagonal. One move too late, if the next move stands.

The clamp: c5 is now a protected outpost pawn cramping Black's whole queenside, and ...Bxc5 no longer exists. What you owe in exchange is care over ...a5 — the undermining move that is the entire counterplay from here.

The direct regain: the f8 bishop will take on c5. This is the moment to decide which plan you are in — the checkpoint above this line asked you, and this branch is where 'return it at a price' plays out.

Not a holding move. Mechanically verified this session (chessops + Stockfish 18, depth 22): after 5.Be3 the immediate 5...Bxc5 is answered by 6.Bxc5 and Black has no legal recapture on c5, leaving Black a bishop down at +4.54 for White. What Be3 does here is defend c5 with a piece; what happens next is not authored in this pack.
Declining the pawn is playable — but see what Black gets for free: the break has already succeeded, and the tension is Black's to resolve.
Black liquidates the base at no cost.

A fine, slightly better-for-nobody middlegame: the knight is central, e5 still cramps, but Black solved the problem the Advance exists to pose — without spending the bishop tempo the main line charges. Compare this branch against the capture and decide which game you would rather have.

Propping the base looks principled and concedes the point: after ...cxd4 cxd4 the break has traded itself off for free, Black's queenside is unweakened, and your extra space must now win the game on its own. Authored as a branch precisely so you can feel the difference from the capture.

checkpoints.label: Pawn in hand — hold it or sell it?
b4 — the pawn is held and the target is now a5
The declined version — what Black got for free
c3 — the break traded itself off at no cost
You are past the authored line

deviations.note: 5.Bb5 pins the regaining knight and fights for the c5 pawn tactically. Sharper than the spine's development order; after ...Qa5+ ideas both sides must know concrete lines, which is exactly the invitation this pack's plan declines to send.
5.Be3 offers the same exchange logic as the ...e6 branch one move earlier: hold with a piece, and if ...Ng4 or ...Qa5+ come, the concrete lines hold up. Equivalent plan, different move order.

5.b4 holds the pawn with pawns before a single piece is developed. ...a5 hits immediately and every defence of b4 costs another non-developing move — the exact debt spiral the spine's c3-first order avoids. The extra pawn is not worth being three tempi behind in an open position.
5.Nf3 first, deciding about the c5 pawn only after seeing Black's next move. Loses nothing and commits to nothing; the spine plays Be3 first only to make the exchange-offer idea explicit.

5.Qg4 exploits the one drawback of ...e6 — the c8 bishop no longer guards g7's diagonal escort, so the f8 bishop must choose between g7 duty and taking on c5. An early queen sortie with real bite here; it also hands Black developing moves with tempo if mishandled. Play it out before trusting it.
6.Be2 breaks the pin before bracing. Solid, one beat slower on the queenside; against it Black's ...e6 regain arrives with the b4 clamp not yet available.

6.b4 clamps immediately, without c3 behind it. Now ...a5 comes with ...axb4 and there is no c3 pawn to recapture toward the centre — the same clamp, structurally weaker by exactly one preparing move. A concrete illustration of why move order is the pack's subject.

feedbackClaims.text: After 3.e5 at the 1400/1600/1800 rating bands (Lichess blitz+rapid, 2024-01 through 2026-07), the immediate 3...c5 is Black's choice in 30.0% of 9,346,096 games — nearly one Advance Caro-Kann in three skips ...Bf5, so an Advance repertoire without an answer here is a third unprepared.

The capture's justification is a tempo ledger, not greed: with the c8 bishop undeveloped, dxc5 costs White nothing, while every Black move spent regaining the pawn is a developing move White gets for free.
After dxc5 this is no longer a pawn-chain opening: the d4-e5 chain is gone, and the game's currency switches from break timing to development lead plus the e5 space pawn.

graduationBlockers.statement: ENGINE-CHECKED 2026-08-15, partly settled and partly destroyed. 5.b4 evaluates 0.88 below the spine's 5.Nf3 at depth 22, and after 5.b4 a5 the position is -0.15 with Black already the better side — the direction of the note holds, while 'three tempi behind' is a count no evaluation produces and stays authored. graduationBlockers.statement: REFUTED AND DELETED 2026-08-15 — the pack's largest single error. The spine line 5.Be3 Bxc5 6.Bxc5 was authored as an even trade ('Material is level again'). It is not: after 6.Bxc5 the only legal capture on c5 was White's, Black has no recapture, and the position evaluates +4.54 for White at depth 22 with material 38-35. Spine nodes bxc5-recoup and bxc5-trade, checkpoint price-collected and the two authoredBoundary entries were removed. No replacement line was authored, because authoring one would be manufacturing chess this pass cannot ground: the return-for-development plan class now names a plan with no line under it.
